newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - FEB 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - FEB 17.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--A joint statement by National Economy and Finance Minister Yannos Papandoniou and Labour Minister Miltiades Papaioannou has failed to extinguish the controversy which has erupted over the government's plans to transfer pension funds' reserve capital - estimated at two trillion drachmas - to the Bank of Greece. Opposition parties, the General Confederation of Workers of Greece, bank and journalists' unions said the move effectively negated the government's intentions for social dialogue, prevents funds from making their own decisions and is a sleight of hand for the government to cover its deficits.

--Striking teachers will kick off the fifth week of their strike with a nation-wide rally in Thessaloniki today. Yesterday Justice Minister Evangelos Yannopoulos said the issue had reached a deadlock and only divine intervention could convince teachers to talk to the education ministry.

--Reports of barbaric dog fights in northern Greece - in which pit bulldogs fight to the death - were confirmed yesterday. Organised by punters betting on the dogs, the dog fights are videotaped and attended by hundreds of spectators. Police said they had arrested four people involved in the organisation of the dog fights.

--Conservative New Democracy opposition leader Miltiades Evert called on Prime Minister Costas Simitis to accept his proposal for the drafting of a united foreign policy strategy and says he will carry the political cost of any joint decisions taken.

--Changes to the social security system will result in a wave of departures. Already, applications for early retirement - primarily by women - have been filed. The anxiety is compounded by the recent news that the government has comandeered pension funds' reserves.
--Shopkeepers around the country will keep their premises locked today in protest at the storm of taxes.
--Kostas Karamanlis, an up and coming New Democracy cadre, left open the eventuality of his standing for the post of ND leader in an interview.

--National Economy and Finance Minister Yannos Papandoniou has predicted loans with an interest rate of less than 10.0 percent in the next few months and inflation below 5.0 percent by the summer. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
